prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: production fantasy RPG atlas texture.
Image 1 is the authoritative exact top-down geographic plan. Image 2 is the authoritative binary land/water mask. Image 3 is ONLY a painterly style reference; ignore all its text, layout, symbols, geography and frame.
Paint the whole known world as one continuous, beautifully hand-painted atlas plate: the autumn southern coast, Momiji Hamlet and its maple woods, the blue-roofed coastal city of Hidamari, the great snowy volcanic caldera, the wooded northern foothills and the pastoral Haras Valley with its racecourse and railway. Deep turquoise sea with layered coastal shallows, soft surf and subtle painted depth. Warm land tones, fine ink contours, delicate roof plans, individually readable tree crowns. Classic hand-illuminated adventure atlas, not a satellite photograph and not a game minimap.
STRICT CAMERA: orthographic top view, north up, looking vertically down. No perspective, no horizon, no isometric buildings or mountain silhouettes. Circles remain circles. No rotation, recentering, zoom, crop or changed scale.
GEOMETRY: preserve Image 1's exact frame, coastline, land/water mask, islands, road and rail alignments, city street grid and building footprints, racecourse, caldera position and every landmark footprint. Image 2 overrides all artistic interpretation of the coast. Do not invent towns, roads, rivers, islands or mountains.
REMOVE TILE SEAMS: Image 1 contains large straight-edged rectangular tint boundaries from terrain data products, especially a square around Haras Valley, a rectangle around the volcanic highlands, and a translucent rectangle over the western hills. These are rendering artifacts, NOT real borders. Blend them away completely into continuous terrain. There must be no straight-edged rectangular colour changes, no hard tile boundaries and no visible product seams anywhere. Preserve the real contours and terrain inside those areas.
WATER SEMANTICS: only saturated blue/cyan shapes in the plan are water. Muted grey/green/brown closed contour rings are DRY HILLTOPS, never lakes. White is snow or concrete, never water. Do not flood the caldera or northern depressions. Preserve the river and coastal water exactly.
NO TEXT OF ANY KIND: no letters, numbers, place names, title, legend, compass rose, banners, scrolls, map pins, icons, badges, borders or UI. All names are live overlays. Fill the entire image with map terrain and sea; no decorative margins. High finish, fine paper grain, crisp paths, restrained contrast, readable at game UI scale.

painted_record.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: production fantasy RPG atlas texture.
Image 1 is the authoritative exact top-down geographical plan. Image 2 is the authoritative coast mask. Image 3, if present, is ONLY a painterly style reference; ignore all its text, layout, symbols and geography.
Paint this plan as a beautiful, richly detailed hand-painted adventure atlas, with the clarity and craft of a classic World of Warcraft regional map. Warm parchment undertones, fine ink contours, softly shaded olive forests, earth and ochre paths, delicate roof plans, turquoise water with subtle coastal depth. An elegant, cohesive painted world, not a satellite photograph.
Scene: A sheltered pirate cove opening south onto the turquoise sea: a horseshoe harbour with timber piers and a shipyard slip, a cobbled market square, a waterfront of colourful plastered houses climbing in terraces up the hill, a watchtower on the ridge, a red-and-white lighthouse on the western headland, and a river gorge with a two-tier waterfall on the eastern headland. Tropical jungle and palms on the headlands. Preserve the exact cove outline, piers, streets and roof footprints. All water stays open sea: no ships, boats, rocks or islets anywhere outside the land of the mask; the game draws its moored galleons and sea stacks itself.
STRICT CAMERA: orthographic TOP VIEW, north up, looking vertically down. No oblique view, no perspective, no horizon, no isometric buildings or mountain silhouettes. Mountain relief is shaded contour/rock texture seen directly from overhead. Circles remain circles. No camera rotation, recentering, zoom, crop or changed scale.
GEOMETRY: preserve the first image's exact frame, coastline, land/water mask, river courses, road and rail alignments, islands, building positions and landmark footprints. Keep the empty sea where shown. Paint detail within those shapes; do not invent towns, bridges, rivers, islands, roads or mountains. Rectangular tint boundaries in the plan are rendering-layer seams: blend their colours naturally while preserving contours and physical geography. The first image always overrides the style reference.
WATER SEMANTICS: only clearly saturated blue/cyan shapes in the plan are water. Muted grey/green/brown closed contour rings are DRY HILLTOPS, never lakes. White is snow or concrete, never water. Do not turn any northern contour depression or the volcanic caldera into a blue lake. Do not extend the river beyond its precise drawn course. Preserve exact roof/park geometry rather than inventing rock towers.
NO TEXT OF ANY KIND: no letters, numbers, place names, stable names, title, legend, compass rose, banners, scrolls, map pins, icons, badges, borders or UI. All names and destinations will be rendered by the game as editable live overlays. Fill the entire image with the map terrain; no decorative margins. High finish, subtle fine paper grain, crisp paths, restrained contrast, clear terrain at game UI scale.
SHORELINE CORRECTION: Image 2 is an authoritative binary terrain mask: WHITE is solid ground, BLACK is water. Match its silhouette at the exact same pixel positions; do not enlarge, shrink, recenter or rotate the land. Paint terrain only inside the white footprint. Surf is water, not extra dry ground. If image 3 is present, it is STYLE ONLY: its shoreline is older and must not be copied. The binary mask overrides all artistic interpretation of the coast.
